To view a copy of this licence, visit http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . We have been using sportomics to understand hypermetabolic stress. Cross Combat (CCombat) has recently been initiated as a high-intensity functional training method inspired by CrossFit. We used a CCombat session to induce metabolic stress and evaluated its effects on hydration and kidney function. Blood samples were collected from 16 elite-level professional male athletes engaged in training sessions over a 96-h protocol. Blood myoglobin increased by ~ 3.5-fold (119 ± 21 to 369 ± 62 nmol/L; p = .001) in response to the protocol, returning to the pre-exercise level within 48 h. Furthermore, d -dimer levels increased from 6.5 ± 0.6 to 79.4 ± 21.3 μmol/L ( p < .001) in response to exercise decreasing during recovery with high variability among the studied athletes. Albuminemia and creatininemia increased ~ 10% and cystatin C increased ~ 240% (1.7 ± 0.1 to 5.7 ± 0.5 mg/L; p < .001; effect size = 2.4) in response to the protocol. We measured albuminuria (HuA) to assess kidney permeability to albumin caused by exercise. HuA increased ~ 16-fold (0.16 ± 0.03 to 2.47 ± 0.41 μmol/L; p < .001; effect size = 1.4) in response to exercise, dropping and reaching basal levels during 48 h. Here, we suggest that microalbuminuria can be used as an early, sensitive, easy, and inexpensive biomarker to evaluate hydration status changes during intensive exercise, decreasing chronic impairment in renal function. Subject terms Biochemistry Diagnostic markers Predictive markers Kidney Brazilian Olympic Committe (BOC) Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico (CNPq) Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (CAPES) Financiadora de Estudos e Projetos (FINEP) Fundação Carlos Chagas Filho de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (FAPERJ) Merck-Sigma-Aldrich Universidade Federal do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (UNIRIO) Waters Corporation issue-copyright-statement © The Author(s) 2022 Introduction Sportomics is a subject-centered holistic method that focuses on sports as the metabolic challenge 1 (for an editorial and reviews, see Bragazzi 2020; Bassini and Cameron 2014; Sellami et al. 2022) 2 – 4 . In addition, the use of metabolomics is rapidly gaining space in understanding exercise and sports 5 . We have been utilizing sportomics and other in-field exercise models to understand hypermetabolic stress in health and disease 2 , 3 . Unlike the studies carried out in the laboratory under controlled conditions, sportomics involves samples collected in the field, enabling us to capture important temporal physiological changes during training and competition. Although in-the-field measurements are inherently less controlled and thus more variable, sportomics leads to reproducible results with high sensitivity 6 – 8 . High-intensity functional training (HIFT), like high-intensity interval training (HIIT), is a new training modality that mixes high-intensity exercises with functional movements, and CrossFit (CFit) training has emerged as the most common and growing form of HIFT worldwide 9 , 10 . It has been proposed that HIIT is the essence of combat sport-specific training 11 . Cross Combat (CCombat), a new method inspired by CFit, has recently been initiated as a training method using specific fighting movements. CCombat is divided into three specific training levels: beginner, intermediate, and advanced. In the beginners' group, the cargo is the body mass itself, whereas at subsequent levels, auxiliary equipment common to traditional CFit is added to fighting movements. Unfortunately, many reports have linked CFit training to severe mechanical injuries or life-threatening conditions, such as rhabdomyolysis 12 , 13 . Adequate hydration is a central biological issue, and inadequate fluid intake associated with intensive exercise programs has been associated with harmful conditions, such as rhabdomyolysis and the impairment of renal filtration 14 , 15 . The first reports of rhabdomyolysis in the modern era occurred during World War II, and some biblical references are related to the disease (for a review, refer to Zager 16 ), and hydration can both prevent and treat this condition 17 , 18 . The evaluation of nitrogenous compounds such as creatinine, urea, and urate is of great value in daily clinical follow-up; however, the elevation of these parameters in the blood is already a consequence of the impairment of renal filtration. To assess kidney function, the experimental gold standard is the measurement of either inulin or iothalamate clearance 19 , 20 , although it has not been used in clinical practice. In this context, the discovery of physiological early markers of hydration is crucial for hydration assessment during metabolic stress. The identification of early and reliable biomarkers of acute kidney levels at either the systemic or cellular level is of great interest for both science and clinical applications 21 . In this setting, we hypothesized that a sportomics approach may reveal new markers of hydration and establish a temporal relationship of onset and washout of these substances. For that purpose, in this study, we used a 40 min CCombat protocol to induce metabolic stress studied under a sportomics approach evaluating the effects of CCombat on hydration and kidney function.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study utilized a sportomics approach to investigate the physiological, biochemical, hemodynamic, metabolic, and hydration parameters in elite athletes undergoing a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) exercise protocol. The main aim was to evaluate the effects of this intensive training on hydration and kidney function, ultimately suggesting albuminuria as a sensitive biomarker for assessing hydration status changes during strenuous activity and mitigating chronic renal impairment.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cross Combat (CCombat), a high-intensity functional exercise protocol inspired by CrossFit
treatment_details.dose_specificity: The protocol involved a 40-minute high-intensity functional Cross Combat (CCombat) session, characterized as a 'cyclic exercise' with high-ATP demand, an intensity level of 70% repetition maximum, and 12 different exercises combined into six modules, designed to induce metabolic stress. Sixteen elite-level professional male athletes were engaged in training sessions over a 96-hour protocol, with blood samples collected. The study was observational, and athletes had free access to hydration post-protocol. No specific dose-response comparisons were reported.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased by ~3.5-fold (119  1 21 to 369  1 62 nmol/L; p = .001) in response to the CCombat protocol, remaining elevated during short recovery and returning to pre-exercise levels within 48 hours (long recovery). Showed a high correlation with CK-MB (r s 0.66 10.86) during recovery.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Oxygen-binding protein released from muscle tissue; indicator of muscle integrity and damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol-induced metabolic stress and subsequent short/long recovery periods (up to 48 hours).
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates hypermetabolic stress and muscle microinjuries following intensive exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly from 6.5  1 0.6 to 79.4  1 21.3  5mol/L (p < .001) in response to intensive CCombat exercise, with increases ranging from 22 to 5.4-fold in 15 of 16 athletes, decreasing during recovery. High variability was observed among athletes, with elevated levels noted at +24 h in one individual.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Biomarker of coagulation and fibrinolysis, also an indicator of muscle integrity and damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Intensive CCombat exercise and subsequent recovery periods.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates physiological stress response, muscle damage, or coagulation activity, emphasizing the need for individualized analysis due to high variability.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased ~10% (ranging from 10-14%) during the short recovery period (SRecover), returning to basal levels during long recovery (LRecover). The increase occurred at the same ratio as creatinine in response to exercise, though with a slight delay.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Major blood protein, sensitive marker of volemia and fluid balance, related to hydration status.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol induced metabolic stress, observed during short and long recovery periods.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Associated with metabolic stress and hydration changes; confirms changes in blood volume/volemia, potentially indicating a last escape of water from the blood in response to exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased ~10-11% in blood in response to the CCombat protocol, returning to basal levels within 24 hours. The increase was at the same ratio as albumin in response to exercise.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Metabolite of creatine, serving as an indicator of renal filtration and glomerular filtration rate (GFR).
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol induced metabolic stress, impacting renal filtration; observed at the end of exercise and during recovery.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates impairment or reduction of renal filtration (GFR) due to intensive exercise, though interpretation can be complex due to muscle damage effects.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly by ~240-250% (~3.4-fold) (from 1.7  1 0.1 to 5.7  1 0.5 mg/L; p < .001; effect size = 2.4) in response to the CCombat protocol, quickly returning to basal levels within the first hour of recovery. Post-CCombat CysC negatively correlated with pre-exercise creatinine (r s -0.71), and showed both negative (r s -0.50 at 60 min) and positive (r s 0.53 at 24 h) correlations with urinary albumin (HuA).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Protein that reflects glomerular filtration rate (GFR), considered a sensitive biomarker of kidney function, less affected by diet or muscle mass than creatinine.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: CCombat protocol-induced metabolic stress, observed at the end of exercise and during early to long recovery.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Sensitive indicator of kidney function changes and glomerular filtration impairment due to intensive exercise and metabolic stress; indicates transient albumin permeability and albuminuria.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Remained constant during rest, but increased significantly by ~16-fold (1600%) (from 0.16  1 0.03 to 2.47  1 0.41  5mol/L; p < .001; effect size = 1.4) in response to CCombat exercise. It dropped during short recovery and reached basal levels within 48 hours (long recovery). Microalbuminuria (MA) ranged from 0.45 to 4.5  5mol over a 24-hour period.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Assesses kidney permeability to albumin, reflecting changes in glomerular filtration caused by exercise.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Intensive CCombat exercise and subsequent hydration status changes, observed during short and long recovery periods.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Identified as an early, sensitive, easy, and inexpensive biomarker for evaluating hydration status changes and acute kidney impairment during intensive exercise, potentially mitigating chronic renal dysfunction and aiding human performance assessment.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: transient decrease followed by no change
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Decreased by approximately 5% during the second rest day (Rest2d) attributed to hydration restoration. It did not change (ranging from 43% to 45%) during the CCombat protocol (0 140 min) or during short (up to 120 min) or long (up to 48 h) recovery. Changes correlated highly with natremia during resting (-48h and -24h), with r s values of 0.65.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Reflects changes in blood volume/volemia and is used as a tool for hydration follow-up in exercise; a decline can be attributed to hydration restoration.
